title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, and Upgrade/Rollback
author: Marta Ruiz
content:
Overview

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It combines: reference architectures, on-prem packaging guidance, the customer requirements library, day-2 operations checklists, and upgrade & rollback procedures. Target audience: solutions engineers, platform engineers, and customer SREs working on private deployments.

Scope

- Supported deployment modes: VPC-managed (customer VPC with Redwood control plane peering) and fully on-prem (air-gapped or customer network).
- Components: control plane, data plane (inference runtime), model registry, metrics/observability stack, KMS/HSM integration, and optional edge routing.

High-Level Responsibilities

- Solutions engineering: customer requirements intake, initial architecture, packaging handoff.
- Eng-private-deployments: packaging artifacts, install scripts, and upgrade playbooks.
- Customer IT/Security: network, firewall, KMS/HSM setup, and host provisioning.

Reference Architectures (summary)

1) VPC-Managed (recommended for most enterprise customers)

- Control plane (Redwood-hosted): API endpoint, metrics ingestion endpoint (TLS), and rollout controller.
- Customer VPC: Kubernetes cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS or self-managed), private ALB/NLB, NAT gateway for egress (if required).
- Networking: TLS mutual authentication for control plane; dedicated peering/VPN between Redwood and customer (IPSEC or AWS Transit Gateway).

Minimum resource table

| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Control plane (customer cluster components) | 4 vCPU / 8 GB | 8 vCPU / 32 GB | depends on predicted concurrency |
| Inference nodes (GPU) | 1 x A10G or equivalent | 2 x A100/4 x A10G | matching model size/throughput needs |
| Model registry storage | 100 GB | 1 TB NVMe | use S3/NFS depending on environment |
| Observability | 2 vCPU / 4 GB | 4 vCPU / 8 GB | Prometheus + Grafana + Loki/Tempo |

2) Fully On-Prem / Air-Gapped

- Control plane runs as customer-managed bundle. A minimal control plane provides local orchestration, rollout controller, and model artifact serving.
- Packaging delivered as signed OCI images + air-gap artifact bundle (tarball + checksums + PGP signature).
- KMS/HSM: HSM connector shim included; integration instructions per vendor (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM).

On-Prem Packaging & Distribution

- Release artifacts: signed OCI images, Helm charts, CRD manifests, and an "airgap" tarball with containerd images and tarred charts.
- Packaging validation: SHA256 checksums, PGP signature, and a manifest.json (fields: version, build_id, images[], checksums[]).

Example manifest.json (airgap)
```
{
  "version": "2026.04.01",
  "build_id": "rdw-deploy-20260401-1234",
  "images": ["rdw/runtime:2026.04.01", "rdw/control-plane:2026.04.01"],
  "checksums": {"rdw-runtime.tar": "sha256:..."}
}
```

Packaging checklist (delivery to customer)

- [ ] Signed OCI images pushed to customer registry (or included in airgap bundle)
- [ ] Helm charts versioned and signed
- [ ] Installation guide and sample values.yaml included
- [ ] Upgrade & rollback playbooks included

Customer Requirements Library (network / security / compliance)

Network requirements (example)

- Outbound: control plane API endpoint (TLS) over 443 (IP ranges to be exchanged during onboarding).
- Inbound: Private ALB/NLB for external client traffic (ports 80/443).
- Inter-pod: Calico/Cilium recommended for network policy enforcement.
- MTU: 1500 (we recommend jumbo frame testing if using RDMA for GPU nodes).

Security & secrets

- KMS/HSM: customer must provide KMS endpoint and credentials; supported providers: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault, Thales HSM.
- Audit logging: ensure long-term retention (>= 90 days) for customer compliance; logs should be exported to customer SIEM.
- RBAC: OIDC integration recommended; map Redwood roles to customer groups.

Storage & backups

- Model artifacts: S3-compatible with versioning enabled; snapshot retention policy: 30 days for active models, 365 days for archival.
- Database: Postgres (managed or self-hosted) for metadata; daily backups, WAL archiving enabled.

Day-2 Operations (runbook and checklists)

Daily health check (SRE quick checklist)

1. Confirm control plane API health: curl -fsS https://control-plane.internal/healthz (expect 200)
2. Check node GPU utilization: rdwctl nodes list; ensure none are > 85% sustained for > 10m
3. Verify recent model loads: rdwctl models status --last 24h
4. Confirm Prometheus alert queue is empty and pagerduty integration OK

Weekly maintenance tasks

- Rotate TLS certificates and KMS credentials per customer policy.
- Prune unused model artifacts: rdwctl model prune --older-than 90d (dry run first).
- Run performance smoke test: run-inference-loadtest --config smoke.yaml (validate p95 latency < defined threshold).

Incident escalation & ownership

- First responder: customer SRE / infra.
- Escalation to Redwood: eng-private-deployments oncall. Use the internal runbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-runbook-2026-03-10

Upgrade procedure (control plane & runtime) — summary
Prerequisites:
- Backup Postgres and model registry metadata (pg_dump + object storage snapshot).
- Ensure all operators and Helm releases are at compatible versions.
- Confirm smoke tests and canary target namespaces exist.

Step-by-step:
1) Announce maintenance window to stakeholders (SLA: avoid top-of-business hours).
2) Create a full backup: pg_dump --dbname=rdw_meta > rdw_meta_YYYYMMDD.sql and snapshot model storage.
3) Deploy control plane minor version to canary namespace (helm upgrade --namespace rdw-canary --values canary-values.yaml rdw/control-plane --version x.y.z)
4) Run integration smoke tests against canary (20 synthetic requests, p95 threshold).
5) If canary passes, rollout to remaining namespaces with a throttled batch (helm upgrade in groups of N clusters/namespaces).
6) Monitor metrics (error rate, latency) for 30 minutes after each batch.
7) If an elevated error rate (> 1% increase in 5m window) or latency regressions (p95 > baseline + 20%), initiate rollback.

Rollback procedure (quick reference)

1) Trigger rollback via Helm: helm rollback <release> <previous_revision> --namespace <ns>
2) Restore metadata if schema-breaking change occurred (use stored SQL dump).
3) If models were reserialized/changed, re-pull model artifacts from archive and validate checksums.
4) Post-rollback: run full smoke tests and update incident ticket with RCA.

Fast rollback decision matrix

- If control plane errors affect > 10% requests or cause > 5 minute outage across > 1 region: immediate rollback.
- If degradation is limited to non-critical paths (metrics tagging only): continue monitoring and schedule patch.

Safe upgrade considerations

- Use non-breaking database migrations with feature flags; avoid rolling DB schema changes and control plane in the same window.
- Provide schema migration playbooks and backwards compatibility matrix in release notes.

Observability & SLOs (suggested)

- SLOs (example for private deployment):
  - Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly
  - Model inference p95 latency (production workload): target depends on model, example p95 < 200ms for small models; p95 < 800ms for large LLMs across batch sizes.
  - Error budget: 0.05% per month for control plane API

Metrics to monitor

- API error rate (5m/1h), median and p95 latency, GPU utilisation per node, cache hit rate (KV cache), model load times, disk I/O saturation, and Prometheus alert rate.

Tooling and CLI snippets

Install (Helm example)
```
helm repo add rdw https://charts.redwood.ai
helm install rdw-control-plane rdw/control-plane --namespace rdw --create-namespace -f values.yaml
```

Airgap load (containerd example)
```
ctr -n=k8s.io images import rdw-runtime.tar
helm install rdw-runtime rdw/runtime -f airgap-values.yaml
```

Validation & acceptance tests (onboarding)

- Acceptance test suite includes: connectivity checks, KMS integration test (encrypt/decrypt roundtrip), model load test, and inference smoke tests with golden prompts.
- Pass criteria: all acceptance checks green; p95 latency within 20% of Redwood hosted baseline for equivalent node type.

Appendix A — Example values.yaml snippets

controlPlane:
  replicas: 3
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 1Gi
    limits:
      cpu: 2
      memory: 4Gi
runtime:
  gpu:
    type: a10g
    count: 2
observability:
  prometheus:
    retention: 30d
